title: Bonus Story: Apocrypha - The Adventures of Brave Peckul
text: My name is Naofumi Iwatani. One day, while rummaging through light novels at the library, I stumbled upon a book called The Four Cardinal Weapons and started reading it. Before I knew it, I found myself thrust into a dream-like scenario—summoned to another world as the Shield Hero, a character straight out of that very book—and thus began my career as a hero in a foreign realm. The trouble was, unlike the other heroes, I knew nothing about this world's particular rules, so the kingdom didn't provide me with any companions. Instead, I was handed a larger stipend and told to go find my own. For the time being, I wandered the castle town, looking for anyone willing to join me, and by the time the sun went down I decided to check into an inn. Today's haul, I suppose, amounted to buying some gear from the old man at the weapon shop and getting on decent terms with him. I managed to purchase a set of chainmail. Obviously I couldn't sleep in it, so I took it off and leaned it against a chair.

I set the pouch of silver coins on the table provided in the room. I'd need to think carefully about how to spend this silver going forward—wages for companions and the like. Feeling a little uneasy about how thin it seemed, I wondered if that was just my ingrained poor-man's instincts talking. Like some tourist stashing cash before a trip abroad, I quietly hid about thirty silver coins inside my shield. Yeah. Somehow that made me feel a bit more at ease.

Quite a day it had been. I'd thought I'd try fighting alone for once, so I went out to the meadow and beat up a monster called a Balloon. So this is what it felt like to defeat a monster, huh. Though "popping a balloon" was really the only way to describe it. I sat down on the bed, then just lay back. An unfamiliar ceiling above me—same as yesterday—reminded me: I really had come to another world.

The excitement wouldn't fade. From here, my glorious days were about to begin. Sure, I was behind the other heroes already, but I had my own path to walk. There was no need to aim for being the strongest; I'd just do what I could. Somehow... I was starting to feel sleepy. Cheerful voices drifted up from the tavern downstairs. I thought I heard something like Motoyasu's voice, and someone who sounded like Itsuki, chatting as they passed by my room. Guess they'd taken rooms here too.
As I was thinking that... knock knock, came a sound at the door. A visitor?
“Yes?”
“Sorry to bother you at this hour, pyon.”
Pyon? What a strange way to end a sentence. Wondering about that, I opened the door, and there was... no one there?
“Down here, pyon.”
When I looked down as instructed, there stood a rabbit, walking on two feet, wearing clothes and a Santa hat, raising one paw in greeting.
“Nice to meet you, pyon. My name is Usaunny, pyon.”
“N-nice to meet you.”

Ah, right—this must be one of those "demi-humans" I'd heard about. Since this was another world, I supposed such races existed here. After all, I knew practically nothing about this world, and even about The Four Cardinal Weapons I only had the vaguest outline.
“You're the Shield Hero, Oto—er, Naofumi Iwatani-kun, correct, pyon?”
The self-proclaimed Usaunny asked, tilting its head slightly.
“Y-yeah. I'm Naofumi Iwatani...”
What was this about? What business could this rabbit demi-human, Usaunny, possibly have with me? Its nose twitched, its ears flicked—kind of cute, honestly.
“I came to ask Oto—Naofumi-kun a question, pyon.”
“A question?”
“That's right, pyon. What does Oto—Naofumi-kun think of fate, pyon?”
“Fate...? I think it'd be wonderful if it existed...”

Being summoned to another world was, in a way, the very definition of fate. Precisely because it was so impossible in reality, it carried a dreamlike quality, and if you painted it with a word like "fate," it seemed all the more wonderful.
“Then which would you prefer—excitement, or none at all, pyon?”
“Well, right now I'd say I want an exciting adventure.”

After all, I'd been summoned as a hero to face down these "waves," these disasters. And honestly, the very fact that I was standing here talking to a rabbit demi-human named Usaunny felt plenty exciting—like something out of a dream. Still... something about this one's voice rang a bell somehow.
“Understood, pyon. Then... I fear you're about to go through something painful, but I want you to remember this, pyon.”
“Something painful...? Remember what?”
“No matter what happens, I will always be on your side, pyon. Now, if you'll excuse me, pyon.”
With that, Usaunny bowed and turned to walk away.
“Ah... one piece of advice, pyon. The more money you hide, the better, pyon.”
“Uh... huh.”

Not really understanding any of it, I closed the door. Seemed like a bit of an odd duck, that Usaunny. Thinking that, I followed its advice anyway and tucked another thirty silver coins into the back of my shield before turning in for the night.

The next day, I woke to find myself stripped of everything I owned, and the pouch of coins I'd left in the room was gone. While I stood there baffled, the castle guards showed up and, before I could even get an explanation out of them, hauled me off to the castle. And there, for some reason, Itsuki stood in front of some woman I didn't recognize, shielding her from my view like he was protecting her.
“Do you truly have no memory of this?”
Itsuki suddenly launched into an interrogation.
“Memory of what... wait, ah-!”
That's when I noticed Itsuki was standing there wearing the chainmail I'd bought.
“You're the one who ransacked my room!”
“Who's ransacking anything! Naofumi-san, I never imagined you were such a scoundrel!”
“Scoundrel? What are you even talking about?”
At my response, the audience chamber took on the mood of a courtroom.
“So then, what is the Shield Hero's crime?”
“Crime? What crime?”
I genuinely had no idea.
“Ugh... hic... the Shield Hero-sama got drunk and suddenly barged into my room, and then he forced himself on me—”
“Huh? Who are you?”
I genuinely, truly had no idea who this woman was. Some adventurer staying in the room next to mine at the inn or something?
“The Shield Hero-sama said, ‘The night's not over yet,’ and came at me, trying to force my clothes off—”
The unfamiliar woman behind Itsuki pointed at me, weeping, condemning me.
“I got so scared... I screamed and ran out of the room for dear life and went to Itsuki-sama for help.”
“Huh? Seriously, who ARE you?”
What was going on? Last night, after chatting briefly with the visiting Usaunny, I'd slept soundly and had absolutely no memory of anything like this.
“Liar! Then why is Kanan-san crying so much!”
“No, seriously, who is that woman! And more importantly, where did you get that chainmail?”
“Ah, yesterday, while we were all having drinks, Kanan-san showed up at the tavern. After drinking together a while, she gave me this chainmail as a gift.”

That chainmail was unmistakably mine, however you looked at it. So this woman had apparently stolen my property and gear while I slept, then gifted it to Itsuki? There was no point reasoning with Itsuki here. I'd bring this to the king instead.
“That's right! Your Majesty! While I was sleeping, this thief stole everything I owned except my shield! Please, arrest that woman!”
“Silence, scoundrel!”
The king dismissed my plea outright.
“Forcing intercourse upon an unwilling citizen of my kingdom is an unforgivable act of savagery—were you not a hero, you would be executed on the spot!”
“I keep telling you, it's a misunderstanding! I didn't do it!”

But everyone present had already decided I was guilty and was proceeding as if it were fact. I felt the blood drain right out of me. What was this? What the hell was this?! Why was I being condemned for something I had absolutely no memory of doing? Gaping like a fish, I glanced at the thieving woman—thinking no one was watching—she stuck her tongue out at me, mocking me. That's when it hit me. I glared at Itsuki. I felt something dark and ugly welling up from the pit of my stomach.
“You! Don't tell me—you framed me for this just to get my starting funds and equipment!”
Pointing at Itsuki, I shouted with a volume that even surprised me.
“Ha! Listen to the sex criminal talk.”
“Don't screw with me! You were after my money from the start, weren't you—coordinated this whole thing to spread the equipment around to your buddies!”
Using someone else's woman-companion to pull off a stunt like this, all to steal my money. Whoever spoke first wins, huh, you bastard!
“To think you'd do something like this to a companion, even after coming to another world—how despicable.”
Ren delivered his cold judgment against me. What was with that composed, detached look on his face?! Look at the situation properly, damn it!
“Indeed. I don't think there's any room for sympathy either.”

Ren and Itsuki condemned me without a shred of hesitation. So that was it... these two had been in on it from the start. Because I had the shield, because I was weak, because I wasn't strong—they'd decided to kick me while I was down, to tilt things in their own favor even a little.

—Filthy. Nothing but cowardly, rotten scum, through and through. Come to think of it, this whole kingdom had never once tried to trust me from the very beginning. Who cared! Why should I protect people like this? Let it all burn! This whole world.
“...Fine, whatever. Just send me back to my own world already, why don't you. Go summon a new Shield Hero!”
Another world? Ha! Why should coming to another world make me feel like this?!
“Running away the moment things get inconvenient? How pathetic.”
“Indeed. Failing to properly fulfill your duties, and trying to force yourself on a woman besides...”
“Get out, get out! We can't keep someone who'd do this as a fellow hero, I say!”

I glared daggers at Ren, Motoyasu, and Itsuki as they spouted their self-serving nonsense, murder in my eyes. This was supposed to be a fun new world. And these bastards had ruined it. For some reason, Usaunny's face flashed through my mind. Was this the "painful experience" it had meant?
“There! Send me back to my own world already!”
At that, the king crossed his arms and groaned.
“I would love nothing more than to send a hero like you back immediately, but there is no method to do so. The researchers say re-summoning is only possible once all the heroes are dead.”
“...Wh-what did you say?”
“No way...”
Only now did Ren and Itsuki look flustered. Motoyasu just stood there silently glaring at me. There was no way back to my own world?
“You mean I can't even go home like this!”
Are you kidding me?!
“How long are you gonna hold onto me, huh!”
I roughly shook off the knight restraining me.
“Hey! Are you planning to resist?”
“I'm not attacking anyone!”
One of the knights punched me. Thwack! Nice solid sound. But it didn't hurt or even itch. The knight, on the other hand, apparently didn't feel the same way, clutching his fist and grimacing in pain.
“So? Your Majesty, what's my punishment supposed to be?”
I asked after swinging my arm around to shake off the numbness.

“...As things stand, since you exist as a countermeasure against the Waves, you bear no formal crime. But your crime has already become known throughout the kingdom. That is your punishment. Do not expect to be employed anywhere in this country.”
“Ohh, how very generous of you!”
So basically, level up as an adventurer and prepare for the Wave, huh.
“You will be summoned for the Wave in one month's time. Criminal or not, you are the Shield Hero. You cannot escape your duty.”
“I know that! I'm weak, remember? I don't have time to waste!”
Just as I noticed the jingle of the silver coins hidden in the back of my shield—
“Wait, I say.”
Here, Motoyasu, as if suddenly transforming into an overzealous soldier, grabbed my collar and shoved me back.
“Ow! Motoyasu, what are you doing!”
Looking at his face... what the hell was this guy doing? Was he coughing up blood? I wiped at a faint trickle of blood at the corner of his mouth.
“This punishment is far too lenient. I shall administer the punishment you truly deserve, indeed.”
“Oho! As expected of the Spear Hero, Kitamura-dono!”
“What are you planning to do?”
Motoyasu held his hand out toward me as I sat sprawled on the ground, and began chanting a spell.
“The Spear Hero, source of power, commands it. Unravel the workings of all creation once more, and transform this one's form.”
“Four Fairy Morph!”
Before I could even process the strange words, some kind of light gathered around Motoyasu and shot straight at me.
“Waaaaaaaaah!?”
With a poof and a puff of smoke, my vision switched in an instant.
“Th-this is...”
“Well I never...”

For some reason, Motoyasu and the others suddenly looked huge. What had they done to me? Looking down, I saw my body had gone strange—my hands had changed into something not human at all, and there was something like fur covering my belly. And further down, right in front of me... a beak!? Motoyasu's giant hand came looming toward my face and I tried to flee in a panic, but with such short legs I couldn't even get up before he grabbed me by the back.
“What is this!? What did you do! Hey! Motoyasu! What did you do to me?!”
“As punishment, you shall spend your days in that form! Fuhahahaha! Now get out of the castle, I say!”
With that, Motoyasu grabbed me, carried me outside the castle, and hooked me on the tip of his spear before hurling it.
“Gungnir!”
“Waaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!”

With a whoosh, I was carried off by the spear Motoyasu had thrown, flung high into the sky, sailing on and on endlessly. In no time at all I went flying—and with an impact like slamming into the ground, my consciousness cut out.
“——I need you to wake up, pyon.”
Regaining consciousness, I opened my eyes to find Usaunny shaking me, a blue sky behind it.
“Where am I...”
I could hear the crash of waves. Was the sea nearby?
“Are you alright, pyon?”
“Ah, yeah... you're Usaunny, right?”
“That's right, pyon. Nao—er, Naofumi-kun.”

Come to think of it, this Usaunny seemed to stumble over its words every time it tried to say my name, didn't it? Shakily, I felt around my face and body with my hands to check what had happened to me. But there was just something like fur, and I couldn't tell much. As I looked around, wondering what had become of me, Usaunny held out a hand mirror, and I took it to check. Reflected there was... a penguin wearing a Santa hat.
“What the hell is this?!”
“It seems Oto—Naofumi-kun has become a peckul, pyon.”
“A peckul?!”
“That's right, pyon. Apparently that's a type of creature, pyon.”
“I-is that so...”
Even being told that, there was no way I could accept this situation!
“That bastard Motoyasu! What did he do to me?! Was that magic or something?!”
Damn it... turning me into this shape out of nowhere—what was the meaning of this?! How was I supposed to turn back? No, actually—wasn't this shape closer to that of a monster?
“Where is this place?”
Looking around, I could tell this was some kind of abandoned village.
“Melromarc Kingdom, Seaetto Territory, Lulolona Village, pyon. It became abandoned due to damage from the first Wave, pyon.”
“I see...”
Looking closely, I could make out traces of monster claw marks and bones and other signs of damage. So a disaster of that magnitude really did exist...
“What on earth happened, pyon? I want you to tell me the circumstances, pyon. I'll lend you my strength, pyon.”
Since Usaunny asked me about the circumstances, I explained everything that had led up to me becoming a peckul.
“That sounds terrible, pyon. No matter what, I will lend you my strength, pyon.”

Hearing that, my heart felt somewhat lighter, in a way. It had said it wanted to help even before I'd fallen into such misfortune, and it believed my current situation. Just that alone was enough to lift me out of feeling like I had no one on my side. Still... I couldn't help but think this world wasn't worth saving.
“Ah... that helps. By the way, something's bothering me...”
Looking at Usaunny's appearance, it struck me—there were a lot of similarities between the small animal wearing a Santa hat and myself.

“I also had my form changed by magic, just like Oto—Naofumi-kun, pyon. The only way to return to your original form is to clear your name of the false charges and have the caster undo it, or to find another way to break the spell, pyon.”
“I see.”

So this Usaunny was also a victim of Motoyasu's, huh. At the time, I just took this at face value without particular suspicion. Later, I'd end up screaming at it, calling it a con artist, but that's a story for another time.
“Looking like this, and falsely accused too—there's no way I can gather companions and get strong... Usaunny, what about you?”
Setting the false charges aside, was there really anyone out there who'd help a guy who looked like a penguin? No way, right? The very idea of being a hero in this state was a joke.
“Due to the effects of the curse, I would hinder Na—Naofumi-kun's growth, so I can't fight alongside you, pyon.”
Tch! So the same restriction that keeps heroes from fighting alongside each other applies here too, huh.
“But I can help you in other ways, pyon.”
“Such as?”

“I'll buy up the goods that Na—Naofumi-kun gathers and sell them, pyon. I think I can sell things much better than Naofumi-kun, given how notorious your name has become, pyon. I'll also bring various other supplies for you to buy, pyon.”
“So basically you're saying you'll act as a merchant and handle things in my place?”
“That's right, pyon.”
“I see...”
Given that Usaunny was under a similar curse, I couldn't very well demand any more from it than that. Just having its help was better than nothing, I supposed.

“I'll also teach you all sorts of knowledge I've gathered about the Legendary Weapons, pyon. If you master how to use that shield's powers properly, you could become far stronger than the other heroes, pyon.”
“That helps. For now... I need food, money, and to level up...”

Whatever else, nothing would start without leveling up. But my stats hadn't changed much even after becoming a peckul. If anything, had I gotten weaker? My level hadn't gone up, at least. If there were any Balloons around, I'd love to punch something and grind some experience. I was itching to take my frustrations out on something. But with this body, I was slow, and punching wouldn't do much anyway. For now, I took out the silver coins I'd hidden inside my shield and showed them to Usaunny.
“Is there anything I can buy with this?”
“Plenty of things, pyon. Let me show you the list, pyon.”

Usaunny showed me a list of goods it could procure. ...Written clearly in copper and silver coin values, which helped a lot. It could even buy fish and such from me for resale. A pretty handy merchant, this one.
“If I can find some cooking equipment usable in this abandoned village, life shouldn't be too hard to manage... For now, might as well dive into the sea. I am a penguin, after all.”
“I'll go find some medicinal herbs and the like, pyon.”
“Alright, see you later.”
With that, I waved to Usaunny and dove into the sea.

Hmm... oh, as expected of a penguin, I could swim through the water exactly as I imagined. There were fish in the sea, and I could catch them easily. Fish I'd never seen in Japan, but I caught a few anyway, went back to shore, found a basket in the abandoned village, and stored them there. When I put some in my shield too, a new shield unlocked. Since it came with effects like improved fishing quality, I switched to it right away.
“I can just keep on swimming and swimming...”

As I swam, probably due to damage from the Wave, I spotted decomposing corpses on the seafloor here and there, which was pretty chilling. Further down in the depths swam monsters I clearly couldn't beat. For now, I figured I should focus on leveling up by fighting weaker fish-monsters found in the shallows.
“And then...”
After securing a decent amount of fish, I went ashore and decided to explore the area around the village. And then...
Some kind of adventurer or traveler with animal ears sprouting from their head noticed me. I braced myself somewhat warily, when—
They dashed straight at me, scooped me up, and started running.
“What are you doing! Let go!”

Dash, dash, dash! Wasn't this person trying to kidnap me!? Worse, they stuffed me into a sack and tied it shut. Being suddenly kidnapped—what was going on?! I couldn't tell the difference in this world between monsters and people with animal ears, but given my current form was closer to a monster than a demi-human, was I being captured alive as a "talking monster"?!
“Guah!?”
As I thrashed about struggling, I took a heavy blow and lost consciousness.
“Mufufu... Father's captivating belly, pyon...”
When I came to, Usaunny had its face buried in my stomach. What was it doing? Was the texture of penguin fur really that comfortable?
“Are you alright, pyon?”

Pulling away with an innocent expression, Usaunny said this as if nothing had happened. It seemed to intend to pretend the previous action never occurred. Looking around, I saw we were back in the abandoned village.
“Nao—Naofumi-kun, you were nearly kidnapped, pyon. I managed to save you somehow, pyon.”
“Th-that's a relief, thanks.”
“Are you really okay, pyon? If you don't like it, please leave it to me, pyon.”
“Even so, I can't just keep relying on you for everything.”
“Please leave it to me, pyon. If I put my mind to it, I could bring peace to the whole world all by myself, pyon.”
Usaunny puffed out its chest proudly, but the sight was anything but reassuring. ...Later I'd find out it really could do exactly that, and end up kicking it for it, but that's beside the point.
“Damn it... seems like I might get caught and sold off as some kind of rare beast.”
Whether human or demi-human, I needed to be very careful around people from now on.
“...I could escape into the sea, at least. Guess I'll just have to focus mainly on the ocean.”

And so, with Usaunny bringing various goods and giving me a daily report of sorts, we settled into a routine. When Usaunny sold off the fish I caught, today's earnings came to about three silver coins.
A few days later.
“Haah...”

What was I supposed to do about this bizarre penguin-transformation, fish-catching lifestyle I'd fallen into? Fortunately, thanks to Usaunny teaching me how to reinforce my shield, I'd become sturdy enough to take hits from deep-sea monsters without flinching, but if I couldn't deal any damage back, that didn't get me anywhere. At best, salvage work and catching weak fish seemed to be the extent of what I could manage.
“I've brought some goods for troubled Father, pyon.”
At some point, Usaunny had started calling me "Father." Apparently I resembled its parent somehow.
“Piyo!” “Piyo!”

And somehow, riding on top of Usaunny's head were a white and a yellow baby bird—chicks that looked like the young of some carriage-pulling monster, like a certain famous yellow chocobo-esque creature.
“What in the world did you bring back this time?”
“Reinforcements to help troubled Father—slaves, pyon.”
“Slaves, you say... You've got such a fancy, cutesy look about you, but the stuff you bring back is way too heavy, man.”
“Then allow me to introduce them, pyon.”
This guy said it with a completely natural expression, like it was nothing at all. And so, guided by Usaunny, I was led to one of the houses in the abandoned village.
“First, Entry Number One! I believe she's a raccoon-species young lady, pyon. Extremely weakened, and she suffers from panic attacks where she screams in her sleep.”
“Cough, cough... um, where is this...”
“As it turns out, she's originally from this very village, pyon.”

The person Usaunny led me to was a girl with tanuki ears and a tail. She looked incredibly timid—no way she could fight. And on top of that, she seemed to have a cold. The stiff, frozen expression on her face gave off an unsettling vibe.
“Entry Number Two! That young lady's friend! Also extremely weakened. I've administered first aid, but caution is advised, pyon.”
“Haah... haah... cough cough...”
And this one was, by any measure, a girl weakened by illness. This one was seriously, genuinely not okay. Give her medicine and let her rest!
“Who are you...”

Even if I said I was the Shield Hero, there was no way she'd believe me, and right now I was some mysterious creature called a peckul anyway. Explaining the situation was way too much of a hassle, but what was I supposed to do? And more importantly, Usaunny—choose your merchandise better! There had to be a limit even to human trafficking.
“Just remember me as a peckul for now. I can't promise I'll be much help, but... I can't just abandon you either.”
“And Entry Number Three! A blind tiger-eared girl, unable to walk, suffering from an inherited incurable disease, pyon!”

And this one was wrapped head to toe in bandages. Usaunny... just what exactly do you expect from me? What am I supposed to do bringing me sick slaves who'll never be any use in a fight?! But abandoning them was harsh too, damn it! Are you trying to bankrupt me or something?!
“...I sense someone with a very strong, gentle presence, but... I suppose that means I've been disposed of separately from Onii-sama. Good. At last, Onii-sama can be freed of me...”
She looked like she might die at any moment. Seriously dangerous-looking, and there was no "Onii-sama" anywhere in sight.
“Hey, Usaunny.”
Beckoning it outside the building, I poked Usaunny with my flipper.
“What's supposed to be useful about those three? They're all half-dead!”
The raccoon-species girl, at least, seemed the most functional of the bunch, but the other two were bedridden.
“It's fine, pyon. If Father catches fish and gives them to them, they'll recover quickly, pyon. But slow, bad-tasting fish won't work, pyon. They'll waste away and die, pyon.”
“What kind of old man from the sixth entry of some legendary fantasy game are these kids supposed to be raised by!”

So catching fast fish and feeding it to them would make them healthy and useful as fighters, huh? Sure, it's an RPG cliché that weak characters joining your party have high growth rates, but was that gimmick supposed to actually make these three combat-capable? Shouldn't we be talking about herbs or expensive medicine just to keep them alive at this point?!
“I'll handle registering everyone's slave crests, so Father just needs to focus on catching plenty of fish and bringing them to me, pyon.”
“You, seriously... haah...”

Guess I had no choice but to just go along with it. I'd thought this whole world deserved to burn over that false accusation, but thanks to Usaunny, life itself was somehow manageable, and it kept saving me whenever I was about to get captured by humans. It was buying all sorts of things with the money too—right now was the groundwork phase; I needed to build up as much of an environment as I could before the next Wave hit. Thinking that, I went out fishing again that day and handed the catch to Usaunny, and sure enough, the enslaved girls gradually started to recover. The raccoon-species girl, Raphtalia, screamed at night just as Usaunny had said, and calming her down was quite the ordeal. Still, thanks to her friend Rifana getting a bit better, work around the village started going smoothly. It turned out she really was originally from this village, and she diligently worked hard on the village chores. And so, a little over a week had passed since I'd become a peckul...
That day, as I was swimming in the sea...

I noticed a mysterious black-and-white shadow far out in the water rushing toward me in an instant. Then I realized the shadow was that of an orca, and a certain memory surfaced in my mind. The natural enemy of penguins: orcas.
“Hi—”

I'd let my guard down, since even though I was slow on land, I could move quickly in the water. But no matter how you looked at it, this thing was far faster than me, and huge to boot. It could easily thrash me around and eat me. No, wait—with my reinforced shield, I should at least be able to outrun it! I've got to flee! Turning my back, I tried to make a full-speed escape, but—
I got grabbed. ...Grabbed? How? Turning around, I realized this orca had hands and feet attached to it!? Don't tell me—an adventurer in the water!?
“Damn it! Let go!”
“Ohh my my my.”
Right after that, a mysterious electric shock crackled through my body, and my consciousness faded away.
“Ugh... where am I...”

I opened my eyes, thinking Usaunny had come to save me again, but there was no sign of it, and instead I woke up in some unfamiliar cave-like place. Come to think of it, Usaunny had only ever rescued me on land when it noticed some commotion involving an adventurer—it had never come to the sea. Worse, I found myself locked in a small cage. Damn... I couldn't die here. Back in the village, three young slave girls and a certain increasingly suspicious Usaunny, along with the Filolials, were waiting for me. No matter what, I had to survive! And so began my escape plan—
April Fools' Day
